# An open grid edit is lost when its column changes body, and the unlock wedges a body

## Context

Leaf of #18762, found by #18867's witness arms. The session is keyed by record id and `dataField`, and `grid.Row#applyRendererOutput` embeds the editor into whichever body renders the column. A runtime lock or unlock of the edited column moves it between bodies while the editor is open. Measured on `#grid-cell-editing-pooled` (`test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing`), locking `c3` from inside the App Worker (no pointer, so no focus change ends the edit first):

| Open edit on record 3's `c3`, then | Observed |
|---|---|
| lock `c3` to the start | the editor follows into the start body, with its draft, and survives a vertical pool round trip |
| lock `c3` to the end | no cell embodies the editor. A vertical round trip does not bring it back |
| lock to the start, then unlock | no cell embodies the editor, and `App Worker: vdom update wedged: "neo-grid-body-4" has been in-flight for over 5000ms. Its reply was likely lost — the component will not update again` |

Controls with no open edit: locking and unlocking `c3` renders every `c3` cell in the new body in both directions. Unlocking from the end places `c3` after `c38`, so it renders once scrolled right (by design, not this defect).

## The Mechanism

Measured at `0887e08dd8` (#18887's head), with the App Worker's plugin methods, `VDomUpdate` registrations and `Helper.updateBatch` wrapped, and the main thread's `DeltaUpdates` logged. `neo-grid-body-4` is the center body, `-5` the start and `-6` the end. Three defects compound:

1. **The editor is lost in the diff.** One batch re-renders all three bodies. Its deltas recycle the center cell that held the editor, `{id: 'neo-grid-body-4__row-2__cell-2', innerHTML: 'r3c4'}`, and only then move the editor, `{action: 'moveNode', id: 'neo-textfield-1', parentId: 'neo-grid-body-6__row-2__c3'}`. The `innerHTML` detaches the editor and focus drops to `BODY`, so the move finds no node. The start direction survives because the start body diffs before the center one, so its move lands before the wipe. `vdom.Helper` already defers removals behind moves (`deltas.default.concat(deltas.remove)`). An `innerHTML` switch that replaces old children, including one the same diff moves, stays in the default phase.
2. **The blur commits.** The detached editor's `focusLeave` reaches `onEditorFocusLeave`. `isEmbodied()` answers from the column's new body, which renders the record, so it returns true: `{embodied: true, locked: 'end'}`. `completeEdit()` writes the draft and destroys the editor. The unlock does the same through `focusMove`, with the editor already unmounted (`mounted: false`).
3. **The wedge.** The batch in (1) is the center body's own flight, escalated to the viewport. The editor had merged into it (its `neo-is-dirty` update was in flight), then `Row#applyRendererOutput` re-parented it to the end body's row. `VDomUpdate#getMergedChildIds` walks a bridge path from each merged child up to the owner. From the re-parented editor that walk never meets `neo-grid-body-4`, so it climbs to the root and adds every ancestor. `collectPayloads()` collects the viewport's full tree, the collision filter drops the body's own payload as covered, and the reply carries a vnode for the viewport only. The body's `resolveVdomUpdate()` never runs, so its registration never clears.

## The Fix

An open edit is held for the duration of any lock change, not only one of its own column: a column changing body also shifts the pool slots of the columns beside it. While it is held, no Row embeds the editor, the blur its removal causes is neutral, and once the bodies have swapped columns, the body rendering the column embeds it again. The draft lives in the editor instance, which survives, as it does when a sort or scroll takes the record out of the row pool. This removes all three triggers here: no diff has to move the editor, and nothing re-parents it while it is merged into a flight. ("Held" rather than "suspended": #18892 uses "suspended" for an edit whose cell left the row pool.)

(1) and (3) are engine defects that do not need a grid to fire: #18900 and #18899, each with its own witness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With an edit open, locking the column to either end and unlocking it keeps the editor embodied in the column's current body, with its draft.
- [ ] No `vdom update wedged` or other worker error during either direction.
- [ ] The two `test.fail()` arms in `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingLockedBodies.spec.mjs` flip to passing arms.
- [ ] The fix names its mechanism, measured rather than inferred, in the PR.

## Out of Scope

- Where an unlocked column lands in the column order.
- Locks started by pointer (a header drag moves focus and commits the edit first).
- Focus returning to the re-embedded editor: the same interaction-contract scope as a reprojection after sort or filter.
